questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, which conformation must a diene adopt to undergo a Diels-Alder reaction?

options.misconception: s-trans cannot bring the ends together
that is required for E2 eliminations

questions.explanation: A Diels-Alder reaction requires the diene in the s-cis conformation so that both ends of the conjugated system can overlap with the dienophile simultaneously to form the six-membered ring in a concerted cycloaddition.
questions.hint: s-cis brings the diene termini close together.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, what does the endo rule predict for a Diels-Alder reaction with a dienophile bearing electron-withdrawing groups?

options.text: The electron-withdrawing group ends up endo
The reaction gives an aromatic product

questions.explanation: The endo rule states that electron-withdrawing substituents on the dienophile orient underneath the diene pi system in the transition state due to secondary orbital interactions, giving the endo adduct as the kinetic product.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, for a four-pi-electron electrocyclic ring opening, which mode is thermally allowed?

options.misconception: the sigma bond must rotate to open

questions.explanation: Under thermal conditions a system with 4n pi electrons undergoes conrotatory electrocyclic motion, while a 4n plus 2 system is disrotatory; photochemical conditions reverse these selections.
questions.hint: Four pi electrons means thermal conrotation.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, what happens in a Cope rearrangement?

options.misconception: that is a different sigmatropic order
that is not the Cope reaction

questions.explanation: The Cope rearrangement is a concerted 3,3-sigmatropic rearrangement of a 1,5-diene in which a sigma bond migrates across the pi system, giving an isomeric 1,5-diene through a six-membered cyclic transition state.
questions.hint: Cope is a 3,3 shift of a 1,5-diene.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, what product class results from an aromatic Claisen rearrangement of an allyl phenyl ether?

options.text: An allyl benzene with no hydroxyl

questions.explanation: An allyl aryl ether undergoes a 3,3-sigmatropic Claisen rearrangement to an ortho-allyl cyclohexadienone, which tautomerizes to the aromatic ortho-allyl phenol; if both ortho sites are blocked, the para product forms.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, for a six-pi-electron electrocyclic ring closure, which mode is thermally allowed?

options.misconception: that is not the electrocyclic description here

questions.explanation: A six-pi-electron system has 4n plus 2 electrons with n equal to one, so under thermal conditions its electrocyclic ring closure is disrotatory; photochemical activation reverses the allowed mode.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, if a dienophile has two substituents that are cis, what is their relationship in the cycloadduct?

options.misconception: cycloaddition is stereospecific and retains geometry

questions.explanation: The Diels-Alder reaction is stereospecific, so cis substituents on the dienophile remain cis and trans substituents remain trans in the cyclohexene product because both new bonds form on the same face in one concerted step.
questions.hint: Stereochemistry of the dienophile is retained.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, which feature defines a pericyclic reaction?

options.text: Bond changes occur through a cyclic concerted transition state

questions.explanation: Pericyclic reactions proceed through a single cyclic transition state in which sigma and pi bonds reorganize simultaneously without intermediates, and their stereochemistry is governed by orbital symmetry rules.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, which structural feature makes a diene more reactive in a Diels-Alder reaction?

options.misconception: those lower the diene HOMO and slow it

options.text: Electron-donating substituents that raise the diene HOMO

options.misconception: a diene needs conjugated double bonds

questions.explanation: Electron-donating groups raise the diene HOMO energy, narrowing the gap to the dienophile LUMO and accelerating the reaction; a normal electron-demand Diels-Alder pairs an electron-rich diene with an electron-poor dienophile.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Analyzing the data, thermal ring opening of cyclobutene proceeds by which mode?
questions.explanation: Cyclobutene has four pi electrons involved in the electrocyclic opening, so under thermal conditions the ring opens in a conrotatory fashion, with both termini rotating in the same direction as the sigma bond breaks.
